name: Power I Wedge Left
purpose: Short yardage and the goal line. Nobody blocks a man — the whole line squeezes shoulder to shoulder on the center and pushes. The tailback puts a hand on the center's back and goes wherever the pile goes.

LTE.rule: Close down hard to the man beside you until your shoulder touches his. Push straight ahead. Never look for someone to block.

LT.rule: Close down hard to the man beside you until your shoulder touches his. Push straight ahead. Never look for someone to block.

LG.rule: Close down hard on the center until your shoulder touches his. Low pads, short steps, push.

C.rule: Snap it and fire straight into the nose with your pads under his. You are the tip of the wedge — everybody else comes to you.

RG.rule: Close down hard on the center until your shoulder touches his. Low pads, short steps, push.

RT.rule: Close down hard to the man beside you until your shoulder touches his. Push straight ahead. Never look for someone to block.

RTE.rule: Close down hard to the man beside you until your shoulder touches his. Push straight ahead. Never look for someone to block.

WB.rule: Tuck in tight behind the right end and seal the edge. Nobody comes around the outside and into the back of the wedge.

QB.rule: Snap, hand it to the tailback left now, and stay out of his way. Do not ride the handoff — he is already moving.

FB.rule: Get in behind the wedge and push the tailback. Both hands on his back, legs driving.

TB.rule: Put a hand on the center's back, get your pads low, and follow the wedge. Do not cut, do not bounce, do not look for a hole — the hole moves with you.

coaching_points: Two yards is a good wedge. Do not call it needing four.
It is drawn against the 6-3 because that is the heaviest front the league allows and it is what you will see inside the five.
Nothing in the league rulebook prohibits wedge blocking for 11-man play, but it is the first thing leagues take away. Re-check it every season before you install it.
Coach the shoulders, not the feet. If there is daylight between two linemen the wedge is a line of five men getting pushed backwards instead of one thing moving forward.
Low pads win this and nothing else does. The team that stands up loses.
